summary: Landowner from Bisaccia in Campania who became a laborer and blacksmith in Dunmore, Pennsylvania; father of Mollie Gianetta and John's maternal 2nd great-grandfather.
bio:
Frank Giannetta, baptized Francesco, was born on 2 May 1869 at Bisaccia, Avellino, Campania, Italy, the son of Savino Giannetta, born in 1842, and Angelamaria Fede. Bisaccia lies about twelve kilometres from Guardia Lombardi, the home of other branches of John's mother's family. On 1 August 1896 he married at Bisaccia; he was then 27 and a possidente, a man of property, and his bride, Angelica Ferrantino, was 23, a foundling born at Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi and living in Bisaccia.

He sailed from Naples on the SS Italia and landed at New York about 15 April 1903, though some records say 1906. By April 1910 he was a contractor's laborer living at 134 Sand Street in Dunmore, Lackawanna County, Pennsylvania, still an alien, with his wife, their four Italian-born children Sam, Mariano, Marie and Tony, and two Italian boarders. By January 1920 he owned the house across the street at 133 Sand Street, with a mortgage, and worked as a laborer in the railroad shops; his sons Sam and Marion worked at a coal breaker, and seven children were at home. In July 1920 he declared his intention to become a citizen at Scranton, under the name Frank Gennetti, and was naturalized there between 1920 and 1923. By 1931, when his daughter Carmela, known as Mollie, married, he was a blacksmith.

He was still at 133 Sand Street in May 1933, when his son Joseph married at St. Rocco's, the church of the Guardiese community in Dunmore. He died eleven months later, on 14 April 1934, at Dunmore. By 1940 his widow was head of the household. His name was spelled many ways in America, among them Gianetta, Genett, Gennetti, Janet and Genet. He is John's maternal 2nd great-grandfather.

researchNotes:
Not in the Ancestry tree; identified in Round 2. FS tree LCPG-XKM (14-17 sources): Francesco 'Frank' Giannetta/Genett, b. 2 May 1869 Bisaccia (AV), son of Savino Giannetta (b. 1842) and Angelamaria Fede; immigrated about 1906; naturalized in Scranton (1920/1923, Middle District Court); lived in Dunmore Ward 5 1910-30; died in Dunmore 1934. 1931 marriage license of his daughter: father Frank, a blacksmith born in Italy, living in Dunmore. Round 3 read his Declaration of Intention No. 16537, US District Court, Scranton, 12 Jul 1920, under the name 'Frank Gennetti': born 2 May 1869 'Bisiccio' [Bisaccia]; aged 50; laborer; of 133 Sand St, Dunmore (Mollie's 1931 address); sailed from Naples on the SS Italia, arriving New York c.15 Apr 1903 (FS profile says 1906); last foreign residence Bisaccia; wife Angelina born in Italy. Marriage, Bisaccia, 1 Aug 1896, Matrimoni 1896 act 18 (FS's '1886' is a typo; Round 2 had flagged 1886 as impossible since Angelica would have been about 12): groom 27, possidente, son of the living Savino and Angelamaria Fede; bride Angelica Ferrantino, 23, born Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi, resident in Bisaccia, foundling. paese.app counts 916 US arrivals from Bisaccia 1830-1912, peaking in 1906, the year FS says he came. Bisaccia is about 12 km from Guardia Lombardi.

The 1910 census confirms the 1896 Bisaccia marriage: Francesco 'Janet', 41, said he had been married 14 years. He was then a contractor's laborer at 134 Sand Street, Dunmore, still an alien, living with his wife, the four children born in Italy (Sam, Marianna/Mariano, Marie and Tony) and two Italian boarders ([R4-S2]). By January 1920 he owned the house at 133 Sand Street (with a mortgage) and worked as a laborer in the railroad shops. His sons Sam and Marion worked at a coal breaker, and the household had grown to seven children at home ([R4-S3]). In May 1933 he was still living at 133 Sand Street when son Joseph married at St. Rocco's, the Guardiese church in Dunmore ([R4-S4]). He died eleven months later. The state death index lists 'Francesco Giannett' of Dunmore, died 14 April 1934, file number 36353 ([R4-S1]). By 1940 his widow was head of the household ([R4-S5]).
